name: Boiled Vegetables (Hinkejvu)
instructions: 1. Wash and chop the colocasia, pumpkin, French beans, and mustard leaves into medium-sized pieces.
2. In a large pot, bring a small amount of water to a boil.
3. Add the harder vegetables like colocasia and pumpkin first and cook until they begin to soften.
4. Add the French beans, mustard leaves, green chilies, and salt.
5. Continue boiling until all the vegetables are tender and the water is reduced to a thick, gravy-like consistency.
6. Mash some of the colocasia slightly to thicken the broth and serve hot.
description: Hinkejvu is a staple dish of the Sumi Naga tribe. It represents the Naga philosophy of eating fresh, seasonal, and natural produce. The dish is prized for being oil-free and preserving the original flavors of the vegetables, making it a healthy and essential part of a traditional Naga meal.
